description: Autopilot mode: the state builder (AX/DOM snapshot -> compact typed PageState), the Laya decision engine wrapping @receptron/laya plus a deterministic stub, and the laya_run_goal loop (snapshot -> state -> decision -> execute -> repeat, handling DONE/BLOCKED). Autopilot degrades gracefully to Assist mode when weights are absent. The decision loop stays pure; Playwright and ONNX are guarded at the edges. Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002.
steps: src/state-builder.ts: buildState(goal, snapshot, recentActions) -> PageState. Reuse the Control[] + visibleText/title/url from src/snapshot.ts capture. Produce a NUMBERED list of controls with their current values (mirroring abedinia/laya-web-agent's documented input: goal + title + visible text + numbered controls with current values + recent actions). Enforce Laya limits defensively: cap the number of controls offered as options (<~20 recommended), and keep option strings short so they fit head_max_len (192 tokens) — the engine must never hand Laya an over-length option set (guard here, since systemOne throws otherwise).

src/laya/engine.ts: LayaEngine implementing LayaDecisionEngine using @receptron/laya. load({ modelDir, repo, subfolder, revision, cacheDir, executionProviders }) via Laya.load(...). decide(state) builds two typed questions and calls systemOne: (1) key 'operation' type 'choice' with criteria = the seven operations {CLICK,TYPE_TEXT,SELECT,SCROLL_DOWN,WAIT,DONE,BLOCKED} and instructions describing the goal+state; (2) key 'target' type 'choice' with criteria = the numbered controls (label each option by its index/ref+role+name). Map r.answers.operation.choice + probabilities -> operation + operationConfidence (max prob), r.answers.target.choice + probabilities -> target ref + targetConfidence. Set source='laya'. Respect the input_tokens/limits. Serialize the state deterministically (JSON like Python json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False)) as documented.

src/laya/stub.ts: StubEngine implementing LayaDecisionEngine with available=true, used in tests and when explicitly selected. Deterministic rules over PageState: if a required goal value is not yet filled -> TYPE_TEXT targeting the matching field with high confidence; if all filled and a submit/search button exists -> CLICK it; if a success marker appears -> DONE; if nothing actionable -> BLOCKED. Mirrors how laya-ultrafast tests with a fake. This makes Autopilot fully testable offline without the 1.7GB weights.

src/laya/index.ts: a factory createEngine(config) that returns a LayaEngine when a modelDir/weights are available OR a real download is enabled, otherwise returns a null-available engine (available=false) so Autopilot can detect absence and degrade. Selecting the stub is explicit (e.g., LAYA_ENGINE=stub) for tests/dev.

src/autopilot/loop.ts: runGoal({ goal, session, engine, maxSteps, ... }) implementing the loop: capture snapshot -> buildState -> engine.decide -> if engine not available, return a graceful result telling the client to use Assist tools -> execute the Decision via Playwright (CLICK/TYPE_TEXT/SELECT via resolveRef; SCROLL_DOWN; WAIT) -> append to recentActions -> repeat until DONE/BLOCKED or maxSteps. Keep the pure decision/transition logic separable from the IO so it can be unit-tested with the stub. IMPORTANT: a DONE decision is NOT proof of success — after DONE, run an independent verification of the final page (e.g., check the goal's expected marker) and report verified true/false in the result.

Register the laya_run_goal tool in the server: input { goal: string, url?: string, maxSteps?: number }. It runs the loop with the configured engine and returns a structured transcript (each step's operation/target/confidence/source) plus the final snapshot and the independent-verification result. If weights are absent, it returns a clear 'weights not present, use Assist tools' message (graceful degradation).

Tests: test/autopilot.test.ts drives laya_run_goal with the StubEngine against a local multi-step form fixture (test/fixtures/search-form.html and/or a filters fixture), asserting the loop fills fields, submits, reaches DONE, and that the independent verification confirms the expected final-page marker. Assert literal expected values (not that functions were called). Add a real-weights integration test that is skipped unless LAYA_MODEL_DIR is set.
acceptance_criteria: buildState produces a PageState with a numbered control list carrying current values, and never emits an option set that violates Laya's head_max_len/count limits.

LayaEngine.decide constructs the two typed 'choice' questions (operation + target) and maps systemOne answers+probabilities into a Decision with confidences; StubEngine produces deterministic Decisions from PageState.

laya_run_goal runs the full loop against a local form fixture using the StubEngine and reaches DONE, with an independent final-page verification result reported (DONE alone is not treated as success).
With no weights present, laya_run_goal degrades gracefully and instructs the client to use Assist tools instead of crashing.
test/autopilot.test.ts passes offline with the stub; the real-weights test is present but skipped when LAYA_MODEL_DIR is unset.
verification: Run 'pnpm run typecheck' and 'pnpm run build' with zero errors.
Run 'pnpm run test' and confirm the autopilot loop test passes offline with the stub engine against local fixtures.
Confirm the real-weights integration test is skipped (not failed) when LAYA_MODEL_DIR is absent.
